reason: This passage (Exodus 1:15-22) depicts Yahweh/Elohim in relational and particular terms rather than as a universal, omniscient, and abstract deity. The text shows: (1) God specifically tied to the Hebrew midwives' fear and reverence—not depicted as universally worshipped; (2) no indication of omniscience—God acts in response to the midwives' obedience, not from prior all-knowing awareness; (3) a personal, interventionist God who directly rewards the midwives with houses, suggesting a relational rather than abstract deity. The characterization is of a particular God bound to Hebrew covenant community, active and responsive, rather than a transcendent, impersonal, universal force.
